description:
Who we are: 

At Rover, pets and their people are at the heart of everything we do. We connect pet parents with trusted pet care across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Australia.

Headquartered in Seattle and Barcelona, we’re a values driven, fast-growing tech company focused on building safe and personalized experiences tailored to the needs of each unique pet. We’re investing in AI as a business accelerator and provide every team member access to AI tools in service of creating better experiences for our community.

We are proud to be recognized as a great place to work, having been named among the 100 Best Companies to Work For in Seattle Business Magazine and Washington’s Best Workplaces in the Puget Sound Business Journal. At Rover we’re committed to creating an accessible, inclusive, and welcoming community, which starts with our employees.

Want to make an impact? Join our pack and come work (and play!) with us.


Who We're Looking For:

As a Trust & Safety Policy Manager, you will help to evolve policies, detection mechanisms, and our strategies to keep the Rover community safe. You'll partner closely with our product teams on safety by design, own policies and program management for our content moderation program, and keep sharpening reactive and proactive policies that guide how we respond to issues or risks.

The ideal candidate will leverage their experience in Trust & Safety to help us continue evolving the program and own areas of expertise end to end. You will have experience leading cross-functional efforts, understand how to measure success, and partner closely with Product, Design, Engineering, Operations, Analytics, and Legal to ensure our policies support every moment of the customer journey.

This position is approved for remote work in FL, GA, ID, NC, TX, WA, & MI.

Your Responsibilities:

  • Reactive & Proactive Policy: Own the review of existing policies and practices to identify opportunities and support new business initiatives, with a focus on ensuring our policies support emerging use-cases and identifying new detection signals and enforcement mechanisms to mitigate risky situations. Use data to inform decisions, define success metrics, and measure impact of policy changes. Use AI to speed up policy drafting, evaluation, and data analysis.
  • Safety by Design & Product Partnership: Support product innovation by reviewing new features and designs to flag trust & safety risks and identify mitigation opportunities so safety is built directly into the product. Act as the primary point of contact for assigned product areas and ensure our policies keep pace with product innovation. 
  • Content Moderation: Help support the development of moderation standards, violation categories, and content appropriateness across the platform. Drive improvements in our content moderation policies, and own our content moderation program to track progress, coordinate cross-functional work, and refine policy as new patterns and edge cases emerge. 

    • Your Qualifications:

  • Experience: 5+ years in trust and safety, product or content policy, risk, compliance, or adjacent work (or 3+ years with an advanced degree).

  • Ownership: You run your own portfolio of moderately to highly complex projects, set priorities against team goals, and bring decision-makers in at key milestones rather than every step.

  • Data-Informed Judgment: You define the right metrics, work comfortably with analysts, and weigh quantitative data alongside customer feedback and industry practice. 

  • Trade-off Thinking: You lay out options, second-order effects, and risks when forming a policy recommendation.

  • Clear Writing: You write policies that a reviewer, an engineer, and a customer can all understand and apply, with exceptional grammar and a sharp eye for detail.

  • Influence Without Authority: You build trust across functions and bring stakeholders with different priorities to a decision.

    • Nice to Have:

  • Policy experience in a two-sided marketplace, gig economy, or B2C platform.

  • You've worked with product teams on launches to advise on risks and mitigation options, and can move quickly to support ideation or brainstorming efforts. 

  • Experience owning content moderation policies and workflows, including policy taxonomies and labelling guidelines, human review workflows, and where automated detection tends to succeed and fail. 

  • AI Fluency: You use AI tools in your own workflows and are curious about how they can make trust and safety work faster and more consistent.

  • Familiarity with privacy, biometric, or online safety regulation and how it shapes product and policy decisions.

  • An advanced degree in law, public policy, or a related field.

    • Benefits of Working at Rover.com:

  • Competitive compensation

  • 401k match

  • Long-term incentive plan with a company performance-based cash payout

  • Flexible PTO

  • Competitive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance

  • Bring your dog to work

  • Pet benefits, including $1000 toward adopting your first dog or cat

  • Regular team activities performed in-person and virtually

    • Compensation:

  • In the Greater Seattle area the first-year salary range is $129,139 - $171,755. In Washington State outside of the Seattle area the first- year salary range is $117,399 - $156,141. Additionally, Rover offers benefits to full-time employees.
  • The cash compensation offered for this role will be dependent on the candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, and abilities as demonstrated in the interview and hiring process.
    • At Rover, we’re driven by seeing our people succeed and grow, while doing our jobs better than ever before. We believe the best business outcomes come from a diverse set of perspectives and we’re committed to promoting an inclusive, inventive, and fun environment with amazing employees. We welcome and encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply. 
     
    Rover is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to age, race, color, ancestry, national origin, religion, disability, military or veteran status, sex, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital or partnership status, genetic predisposition, or any other protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state and local laws.
     
    We are committed to work with you to look for reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.
